points.title: 童年启蒙
points.description: 哥白尼出生于波兰托伦的一个富裕商人家庭。他的舅舅卢卡斯·瓦琴罗德是一位主教，对哥白尼的教育产生了深远影响。在托伦，哥白尼接受了早期教育，展现出对天文学的浓厚兴趣。这座城市位于维斯瓦河畔，是重要的贸易中心，这种开放的商业环境可能培养了他独立思考的能力。舅舅作为教会高级官员，也为他日后的教会生涯奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: Born in Toruń to a wealthy merchant family, Copernicus was deeply influenced by his uncle Lucas Watzenrode, a bishop. In Toruń, he received early education and developed a keen interest in astronomy. The city's position on the Vistula River as a trade center likely fostered his independent thinking. His uncle's position in the church laid the foundation for Copernicus's future ecclesiastical career.

points.title: 大学求知
points.description: 哥白尼进入克拉科夫雅盖隆大学学习，这是当时欧洲最著名的学术中心之一。在这里，他接触到了古希腊天文学著作，特别是托勒密的《天文学大成》，同时也学习了数学和医学。克拉科夫大学的学术氛围和人文主义思想对哥白尼产生了深远影响，为他后来的科学革命奠定了基础。正是在这一时期，他开始质疑托勒密地心说的准确性。
points.descriptionEn: Copernicus studied at Jagiellonian University in Kraków, one of Europe's most prestigious academic centers. Here, he encountered ancient Greek astronomical works, particularly Ptolemy's Almagest, while also studying mathematics and medicine. The university's academic atmosphere and humanist ideas profoundly influenced Copernicus, laying the foundation for his later scientific revolution. It was during this time that he began to question the accuracy of Ptolemy's geocentric model.

points.title: 意大利求学
points.description: 哥白尼前往意大利博洛尼亚大学继续学习，主要研究教会法和天文学。在这里，他遇到了著名的天文学家德·诺瓦拉，两人共同观测天文现象，讨论日心说的可能性。哥白尼还学习了希腊语，使他能够直接阅读古希腊天文学家的原著。这段经历对他日后的科学思想形成至关重要，使他接触到当时欧洲最前沿的学术思想和天文观测技术。
points.descriptionEn: Copernicus traveled to Bologna University in Italy to study canon law and astronomy. Here he met the famous astronomer Domenico Maria Novara, with whom he observed astronomical phenomena and discussed the possibility of a heliocentric model. Copernicus also learned Greek, enabling him to read original works by ancient Greek astronomers directly. This experience was crucial to the formation of his scientific thought, exposing him to Europe's most advanced academic ideas and astronomical observation techniques.

points.title: 教会生涯
points.description: 哥白尼回到波兰，在弗龙堡大教堂担任教士。这一时期，他不仅履行宗教职责，还继续进行天文观测和研究。他在弗龙堡建立了一个小型天文台，使用自制的仪器进行观测。哥白尼还担任了医生和行政官员，为当地居民提供医疗服务。尽管工作繁忙，他仍坚持天文学研究，并开始撰写他的主要著作《天体运行论》的初稿。弗龙堡的宁静环境为他的研究提供了理想条件。
points.descriptionEn: Returning to Poland, Copernicus served as a canon at Frombork Cathedral. During this period, he not only fulfilled his religious duties but continued astronomical observations and research. He established a small observatory in Frombork, using self-made instruments for observations. Copernicus also worked as a physician and administrator, providing medical services to local residents. Despite his busy schedule, he persisted in astronomical research and began drafting the first version of his major work, 'De revolutionibus orbium coelestium.' Frombork's tranquil environment provided ideal conditions for his studies.

points.title: 完成巨著
points.description: 在生命的最后三十年，哥白尼专注于完善他的日心说理论。他进行了大量天文观测，计算行星运动，并不断完善《天体运行论》。由于担心教会的反对，他迟迟没有出版这部著作。直到1543年，在临终前，他才同意出版这部革命性的著作。《天体运行论》提出了太阳是宇宙中心、地球和其他行星围绕太阳运行的日心说模型，彻底改变了人类对宇宙的认识，为后来的科学革命奠定了基础。哥白尼的日心说虽然并非完全正确，但它打破了地心说的统治，开启了现代天文学的新纪元。
points.descriptionEn: During the last thirty years of his life, Copernicus focused on refining his heliocentric theory. He conducted extensive astronomical observations, calculated planetary motions, and continuously improved 'De revolutionibus orbium coelestium.' Fearing opposition from the Church, he delayed publishing this work until 1543, just before his death. The revolutionary book proposed that the Sun, not the Earth, was the center of the universe, with Earth and other planets orbiting around it. This completely changed humanity's understanding of the cosmos and laid the foundation for the Scientific Revolution. Although not entirely correct, Copernicus's heliocentric model broke the dominance of geocentrism and inaugurated a new era of modern astronomy.

supporter.zh: 哥白尼被誉为现代天文学的奠基人，他的日心说革命性地改变了人类对宇宙的认知。他敢于挑战权威，以科学实证精神取代了教条主义，为科学方法的建立做出了重要贡献。哥白尼的工作不仅在天文学领域具有划时代意义，更对整个科学革命产生了深远影响，启发了伽利略、开普勒和牛顿等后来的科学家。他的勇气和坚持体现了科学探索的本质精神。
supporter.en: Copernicus is celebrated as the father of modern astronomy, whose heliocentric theory revolutionized humanity's understanding of the cosmos. He dared to challenge authority, replacing dogmatism with scientific empiricism, making significant contributions to the establishment of scientific methodology. His work was not only epoch-making in astronomy but also profoundly influenced the Scientific Revolution, inspiring later scientists like Galileo, Kepler, and Newton. His courage and perseverance embody the essential spirit of scientific exploration.

critic.zh: 批评者指出哥白尼的理论存在诸多缺陷，如未能完全摆脱圆形轨道的概念，未能解释行星运动的不规则性，也未提供确凿的观测证据支持日心说。此外，哥白尼本人也未能完全摆脱传统观念的束缚，他的理论仍保留了某些古代天文学的元素。一些历史学家认为，哥白尼的革命性被后世过度夸大，他的工作更多是对已有知识的重新组织而非彻底创新。
critic.en: Critics point out that Copernicus's theory had numerous flaws, including its retention of circular orbits, failure to explain irregular planetary motions, and lack of conclusive observational evidence for heliocentrism. Additionally, Copernicus himself could not completely break free from traditional concepts, as his theory still contained elements of ancient astronomy. Some historians argue that the revolutionary nature of Copernicus's work has been exaggerated by later generations, seeing it more as a reorganization of existing knowledge than a radical innovation.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，哥白尼被视为科学革命的先驱和象征。他的日心说虽然不是完全正确的理论，但它代表了人类认知宇宙方式的根本转变，从神学中心主义向经验科学方法的过渡。哥白尼的工作体现了文艺复兴时期人文主义精神与科学理性的结合，他既是一位虔诚的教士，又是一位勇于探索的科学家。在流行文化中，哥白尼常被塑造成挑战权威的英雄形象，象征着人类对真理的不懈追求。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Copernicus is regarded as a pioneer and symbol of the Scientific Revolution. Although his heliocentric theory was not entirely correct, it represented a fundamental shift in humanity's understanding of the cosmos—from theological centrism to empirical scientific methods. Copernicus's work embodied the combination of Renaissance humanism and scientific rationality; he was both a devout clergyman and a daring scientist. In popular culture, he is often portrayed as a heroic figure challenging authority, symbolizing humanity's relentless pursuit of truth.

self.zh: 在宇宙的中心，太阳安坐在王位上，所有行星围绕它旋转。
self.en: In the center of the universe, the Sun sits enthroned, and all planets revolve around it.

others.zh: 哥白尼是第一个将宇宙从人类手中夺走的人，他将人类从宇宙中心的位置上驱逐出去。
others.en: Copernicus was the first to deprive humanity of the universe by removing Earth from the center of the cosmos.
